transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise

A horrible noise in a washing machine is usually caused by one of three things: an unbalanced load or incorrect programme setting, something caught in the drain pump, or worn mechanical parts like bearings. To narrow this down quickly, could you tell me when exactly the noise happens (during wash, draining, or spinning) and what it sounds like (grinding, rattling, or loud banging)?
It's mostly when it spins, a loud roaring rumble like a jet engine. A little noisy in the wash but much worse on spin.

A loud roaring rumble that gets worse as the spin speed increases is a common sign of worn drum bearings. This happens when the seals inside the drum fail, allowing water and grit to damage the bearing race, which then grinds loudly under load. To confirm this, please unplug the machine first. With the door open, push the inner drum firmly downwards and try to lift it up again. If there is significant play—meaning the drum drops down or knocks against the sides before resistance kicks in—that points strongly to failed bearings. If it feels firm and solid with no loose movement, we should look at other causes like a slipping belt or motor issue.
Ok I unplugged it and tried. Yes there's a noticeable clunky up and down movement when I lift the drum edge. Also it grinds when I spin it by hand.

The clunky play and the grinding noise when you turn the drum by hand confirm that the drum bearings have failed. Fixing this requires checking the bearings (and usually the spider assembly), which involves dismantling the entire outer tub—a job for a qualified engineer as it is complex and heavy work. Please do not continue using the machine, as the bearings could seize or the drum could detach during a high-speed spin, causing further damage or safety risks.
